chunks: that a believer should regard lawful this year what he regarded lawful in the previous year, and should consider unlawful this year what he considered unlawful in the previous year.
Certainly people’s innovation cannot make lawful for you what has been declared unlawful;
rather, lawful is that which Allāh has made lawful and unlawful is that which Allāh has made unlawful.
You have already tested the matters and tried them; you have been preached by those before you. Illustrations have been drawn for you and you have been called to clear fact.
Only a deaf man can remain deaf to all this, and only a blind man can remain blind to all this.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on religious innovation (bid'ah) and continuity of halal and haram?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) grounds this exhortation in the concept of *istishab* (presumption of continuity), affirming that the legal status of matters remains unchanged unless explicitly altered by Divine revelation, thereby countering the tribal and cultural innovations (*bid'ah*) that had begun to obscure pure Sharia. This passage serves as a foundational critique of subjective human reasoning in jurisprudence, asserting that true halal and haram are exclusively determined by God, not by the evolving customs of the people. It calls for intellectual clarity, warning that those who ignore these clear, established truths do so out of willful blindness or deafness to the evident signs.
